articles.title: Teacher allegedly filmed hundreds of kids using toilets
articles.description: A primary school teacher has been accused of secretly filming young children as they used the school bathroom more than 357 times on hidden spy cameras. Timothy Blamires, 33, appeared before Melbourne Magistrates' Court on Friday 9 October, for a brief hearing before his matter was adjourned to November 20. Charge sheets released by the court revealed the extent of the teacher's alleged crimes committed over six months at Kingswood Primary School, at Dingley Village. Blamires is accused of installing the spy cameras inside fragrance dispensers in school toilets and filming children between October 13, 2025 and April 21. Court documents allege he recorded "in excess" of 34 prepubescent children on October 13, 2025, more than 188 children a week later on October 20, and over 60 children two days after that on October 22. On March 30, he is accused of recording in excess of 74 children using the spy cams. A cleaner replacing an odour dispenser's fragrance inside the male toilets on April 28 allegedly discovered the hidden camera inside, which had a wire connected to a hard drive. She placed it into a plastic bag and put it on the principal's desk before police were called. While officers were on their way, Blamires is accused of taking the camera and putting it inside a drawer in a sick bay before returning to his class to teach. The odour dispenser was allegedly found inside his backpack at the school after his arrest, and police seized devices from his home including laptops, phones and tablets. Blamires has been charged with 16 offences, including six counts of installing a spy cam, five counts of producing child abuse material, four counts of possessing child abuse material and one count of refusing to comply with a police direction to hand over access codes to devices. He was denied bail in May after a magistrate found his risks could not be reduced to an acceptable level, pointing to difficulties in enforcing a ban on internet access. 1800 RESPECT (1800 737 732) National Sexual Abuse and Redress Support Service 1800 211 028

pendingReview.title: Nurse files FIR against hosp staff for rape
pendingReview.description: Jaisalmer: A nurse employed at a private hospital in Barmer has lodged a complaint at the women's police station, accusing the hospital owner, a doctor, the hospital manager and other staff members of rape and sexual harassment. Police registered the FIR on Oct 8 and have begun an investigation into the allegations.The complaint comes several months after the doctor filed a case against the nurse on July 22, 2026, alleging honey-trapping and blackmail. The nurse was arrested in connection with that case and remained in jail until her release on Sept 30. She subsequently filed the present complaint on Oct 8.In her statement, the nurse alleged that the doctor and hospital owner secretly captured objectionable photographs and videos of her through a hidden camera installed in a changing room while she was changing clothes during her delivery. She claimed they later informed her about the recordings and allegedly used them to coerce her into a sexual relationship, threatening to make the material public.She further alleged that in Jan 2024, while on night duty, she was taken from the labour room to another room and sexually assaulted after being threatened with the release of the photos and videos. According to her complaint, the incident was also recorded, and she was repeatedly threatened with the circulation of the footage and harm to her children. The nurse claimed that she was regularly assigned night shifts and subjected to continued sexual exploitation. Fearing further abuse, she said she stopped reporting to work on March 4 and informed the doctor of her decision through a message.However, she alleged that the doctor later visited her residence and threatened to take his own life if she did not return to work. She claimed she resumed her duties under pressure and that the alleged sexual abuse and physical assaults continued.The complainant also alleged that the doctor sent her explicit videos of himself. She further stated that in May 2026, while the doctor was abroad, the hospital manager and another individual allegedly threatened and sexually assaulted her on May 10. According to the complaint, a female staff member who attempted to help her was threatened with termination.The nurse said she had informed her brother and other hospital employees about the alleged incidents. She further claimed that the doctor later shared the videos on social media and filed the honey-trapping and blackmail case against her in retaliation.Additional Superintendent of Police Nitesh Arya confirmed that a rape complaint had been filed against a doctor, a manager and another staff member. He said the matter is under investigation, and the complainant will undergo a medical examination before her statement is formally recorded.The case is being investigated by the additional SP attached to the women's cell. The allegations remain unverified and are subject to the outcome of the police investigation.

pendingReview.title: Purdue student arrested in Owen Hall voyeurism case
pendingReview.description: A Purdue student was arrested Friday in relation to a voyeurism case at Owen Residence Hall. Jaden Van Vactor, a sophomore in interdisciplinary studies, was arrested after Purdue police received a call around 1:30 p.m. about a suspicious person in the hall, according to PUPD Captain Song Kang. While searching the building for an unescorted male, officers reportedly found the 19-year-old Van Vactor trying to evade the scene, Kang said. After a "brief scuffle," officers apprehended Van Vactor, and he was booked into the Tippecanoe County Jail around 6:30 p.m. Kang said that while evidence is still being collected, Van Vactor is suspected to be the same person who reportedly video recorded or took photos of a woman in a shower in Owen Hall on Sept. 9. Van Vactor has been preliminarily charged with voyeurism, battery on law enforcement and resisting law enforcement. He is being held on a $500 cash bond, according to jail logs. Purdue University spokesperson Trevor Peters confirmed that Van Vactor is a Purdue student and has been suspended. Crime State Sen. Ron Alting accused of shoplifting
